docs.creator: Gustavus Myers
docs.description: LibriVox recording of History of the Great American Fortunes Vol. 3 by Gustavus Myers. Read in English by Celine Major. History of the Great American Fortunes, Volume III by Gustavus Myers is the concluding volume of Myers’s three-part examination of how enormous fortunes were accumulated in the United States. Volume III argues that America's great fortunes were not simply the result of individual entrepreneurship or talent, but were built within a system that enabled powerful financiers and industrialists to accumulate extraordinary wealth and influence. Myers portrays the growing concentration of capital as being supported by corruption and favorable legislation, while ordinary citizens and workers bore much of the economic cost. - Summary by Celine Major For further information, including links to online text, reader information, RSS feeds, CD cover or other formats (if available), please go to the LibriVox catalog page for this recording. docs.creator: Alfred John Church
docs.description: LibriVox recording of The Burning of Rome by Alfred John Church. Read in English by LibriVox Volunteers. The Rev. Alfred J. Church, who has made a good reputation by his stories of life in the Biblical and classic world, adds to his laurels by a fresh volume entitled 'The Burning of Rome.'. It is a story of the days of Nero, and shows how the Christians and pagans lived and thought, and how the new religion gradually displaced the old in the minds and hearts of converts. The basis of the narrative is the historical writing of Tacitus, and Mr. Church's ambition seems to lie in close adherence to the probabilities. He has studied minutely the letters of Paul the Apostle, and seeks wherever practicable to link together the names of persons in the Epistles to places and incidents in Roman history. Epicharis, the chief character, is somewhat idealized. The story is moderately exciting, and may be recommended to Sunday-school libraries, and to all who would know how the Christians lived in the days when there was civilization but no Christian church edifices. - Summary by The Critic, 1891 Cast of Characters: Narrator: Cbteddy Subrius Flavius: JakeTheTank Plautius Lateranus: Colfox The Emperor Nero/Phlegon: Beeswaxcandle Pomponia Graecina: Belinda McReynolds Marcus Annius Pudens: E. docs.creator: Various
docs.description: LibriVox recording of Harper's Young People, Vol. 01, Issue 46, September 14, 1880 by Various. Read in English by LibriVox Volunteers. Harper's Young People is an illustrated weekly publication for children that includes short stories, tales from history, natural history, poetry, puzzles, and other entertainment. This 46th issue of the serial was published on September 14th, 1880. In this issue, a new serial story begins in which Mr. Morton's Select School is joined by a mysterious new pupil who leaves all the students wanting desperately to know, "Who Was Paul Grayson?". Also in this issue, readers missing "The Moral Pirates" of past issues will love the nautical nonsense of the boy sailors in "The 'Longshore Yacht Club"; an adventurous story in which a young passerby must surmount a building's many obstacles to rescue a very important person when a distress note falls in his path in "Dave's Great Lunch"; and readers get first look at the "newly" published science article all about the chemistry of combustion -- it's hot! These stories and many more are sure to inform and inspire children of all ages. Illustrations from this book can be viewed on Project Gutenberg's publication of this book at: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/29136 . This periodical was published by Harper & Brothers, known today for their publications Harper's Bazaar and Harper's Magazine. - Summary by Jill Engle For further information, including links to online text, reader information, RSS feeds, CD cover or other formats (if available), please go to the LibriVox catalog page for this recording. docs.creator: Saint Thomas Aquinas
docs.description: LibriVox recording of The Two Commandments of Charity and the Ten Commandments Of The Law by Saint Thomas Aquinas. (Translated by Henry Augustus Rawes.) Read in English by LibriVox Volunteers. St. Thomas's Treatise on the Commandments is plain, short, practical, and full of instruction. There is a simplicity of strength about it which is to me very attractive. You will see for yourselves how wonderfully the Saint illustrates each point from the Scriptures of God. As with all his writings, so here, the manner is worthy of the words; and the words, so far as man's words can be, are worthy of the truths which they enshrine and unfold. I have added a prayer at the end of each chapter, because the way of the commandments is the way of everlasting life; and we can only go along the road of life by grace; and they who pray find the grace that they need. - Summary by Translator For further information, including links to online text, reader information, RSS feeds, CD cover or other formats (if available), please go to the LibriVox catalog page for this recording.
